- **self**: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) (17/4)

## Definitions

- [statement] A configured oplog size is not a strict disk ceiling: MongoDB can exceed it to preserve the majority commit point. A minimum retention period can also force unbounded oplog growth during heavy writes, potentially exhausting disk. PVC autoscaling still has a configured maximum. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/change-oplog-size/, https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB's documented easy storage expansion requires PVC RBAC permissions and causes a rolling restart of the MongoDB custom resource. Kubernetes and Percona also describe online filesystem expansion without a pod restart when the driver supports it; restart behavior must be checked for the actual controller procedure. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/resize-pv-storage.md · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/percona-operator-volume-expansion-without-downtime/, https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/main/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes.md
- [statement] replSetResizeOplog changes size or minimum retention without restarting mongod, but changes do not replicate to other members. MongoDB's procedure changes secondaries before the primary. Operator-managed deployments therefore need per-member verification when adjusting oplog settings for a migration window. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/change-oplog-size/, https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html
- [statement] MongoDB Controllers’ documented easy expansion updates the MongoDB custom resource, requires PVC permissions in RBAC, and causes a rolling restart. Its manual procedure stops the operator to avoid reconciliation races, orphans StatefulSets, updates the resource, and restarts pods. Do not assume online Kubernetes expansion removes operator-specific restart requirements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/resize-pv-storage.md · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Minimum oplog retention can grow the oplog beyond its configured size and exhaust disk during heavy writes. A Percona operator user independently flags burst-related disk-full risk. PVC autoscaling is only a mitigation: its configured ceiling and the storage provider's expansion support still bound available capacity. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://forums.percona.com/t/feature-proposal-oplog-management/40411, https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html
- [statement] Reducing oplog size does not immediately reclaim allocated disk space. MongoDB documents compact on local.oplog.rs during maintenance to reclaim it, warning that oplog synchronization is blocked. Truncating oplog history can also invalidate change streams or force lagging secondaries to resynchronize, increasing cutover risk. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/change-oplog-size/
- [statement] Reducing the oplog size does not immediately release allocated filesystem space. MongoDB documents compact on local.oplog.rs for reclamation during maintenance; it prevents oplog synchronization. The tutorial says to step down the primary before compacting it. Filesystem reclamation still cannot shrink the Kubernetes PVC. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/change-oplog-size/, https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/
- [statement] Lowering oplog size or retention can truncate history still needed by readers, invalidate change streams or force lagging secondaries to resynchronize. Check remaining history requirements before reducing migration headroom; reclaimed history cannot be recovered by subsequently enlarging the oplog. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/change-oplog-size/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A December 30, 2025 migration report using Percona Operator 1.21.1 found that a 10Gi PVC request against an existing 161Gi local PV failed reconciliation with 'requested storage (10Gi) is less than actual storage (161Gi)'. Treat this as a version-specific migration preflight case rather than assuming ordinary Kubernetes PV binding guarantees operator acceptance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-30) — https://forums.percona.com/t/operator-blocks-pvc-when-requested-storage-pv-size/39954 · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)

## Facts and statements

- [statement] PVC expansion requires an expansion-capable storage class and driver. Kubernetes supports growth, not shrinking an existing PVC; MongoDB's controller also rejects storage decreases during reconciliation. Migration capacity plans should therefore treat a temporary PVC increase as a lasting allocation until data is moved to replacement storage. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/kubernetes/current/tutorial/resize-pv-storage.md · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes) · also: https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/main/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes.md, https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/, https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html
- [statement] Percona Operator 1.23.1 documents threshold-driven PVC autoscaling for replica sets and config servers, introduced in 1.22.0, with a growth step and maximum size. Mongos log PVCs are excluded. Enabling an external autoscaler disables internal automatic resizing; these mechanisms should not be assumed to operate together. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] In Percona's October 5, 2026 storage guide, volume expansion uses spec.storageScaling.enableVolumeScaling and external autoscaling uses spec.storageScaling.enableExternalAutoscaling. Match manifests to the documented operator version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] A March 2026 Percona forum proposal reports that creation-time oplog configuration is declarative but runtime max-size adjustments require manual commands or scripts, with uncertainty after node replacement or physical restore. This is a user's experience and feature request, not proof that every current operator release lacks reconciliation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-30) — https://forums.percona.com/t/feature-proposal-oplog-management/40411 · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] MCK 1.9.1 release notes record a fix for automation-agent-stderr.log growing without bound and filling a PVC; stderr was redirected to pod stdout. Disk-pressure diagnosis should inspect agent logs as well as database and oplog growth. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-03) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-kubernetes/releases · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] Percona Operator 1.23.1 documents automatic PVC growth for replica-set and config-server pods, introduced in 1.22.0. Configure enableVolumeScaling, autoscaling.enabled, triggerThresholdPercent, growthStep and maxSize. Growth stops at maxSize; mongos log PVCs are excluded from autoscaling. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] Percona’s manual replacement procedure can shrink storage by replacing volumes and resynchronizing members sequentially. Its optional temporary increase from three to five members adds compute and storage during the operation; this is a documented procedure, not in-place PVC shrink. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/1.23.1/scaling-storage-resize.html · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
- [statement] A March 2026 Percona forum feature request describes manual runtime oplog resizing and asks for operator reconciliation; a reply suggests considering retention hours and filing a feature request. This thread is evidence of a requested capability, not proof that later operator releases lack oplog management. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-30) — https://forums.percona.com/t/feature-proposal-oplog-management/40411 · keywords: Kubernetes operator PVC resizing and oplog management (Percona, MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes)
